textContent.text: Helen Keller got very sick as a young child. After this sickness, she could not see or hear anymore. So, Helen had to learn words in a different way.

Helen's teacher was named Anne Sullivan. Anne used her fingers to spell out words in Helen's hands. Each letter had a different shape. Helen could feel Anne's fingers making shapes. But she did not know what they meant.
One day, Anne put Helen's hand under some water. Anne spelled the word "water" into Helen's other hand. Suddenly, Helen understood! She learned words for many things this way.
Helen grew up to do many great things. She wrote a book, and she talked to people about her life. Her story showed people that they could work through hard things too.

textContent.text: Mae Jemison always wanted to go into space.
As a child, she looked up at the stars and dreamed of flying there. She also liked to read books about stars and space.

In 1992, Mae set off in a space shuttle. She was on the shuttle for eight days. Part of her job was to learn about what happens to the human body in space. Mae was the first African American woman to go into space.

Diego grew up to be a painter who never stopped making art on walls. He is known for his murals, or wall art.
Diego painted huge murals inside many buildings in Mexico. It was important to Diego to show the life of the people of Mexico. So, he mostly painted wall art of Mexico and its people.
Diego liked painting wall art because everyone could see it. The walls of the buildings were for everyone. Both rich and poor people could enjoy Diego's art.

Jane was the first person to learn that chimps could use tools. She watched chimps get a snack by using branches to get bugs out of holes.
Jane also heard the chimps make sounds like hoots and barks. She learned that chimps use these different sounds to tell things to one another.
Jane shared many things she learned about chimps. Thanks to her, we know much more about these interesting animals.
